problem: Standard pairwise preference optimization for LLM alignment overlooks richer forms of human feedback like multiwise comparisons and ranked preferences.
approach: Ranked Choice Preference Optimization (RCPO) unifies preference optimization with choice modeling via maximum likelihood estimation, supporting both utility-based and rank-based models and subsuming methods like DPO.
contribution: RCPO consistently outperforms competitive baselines on Llama-3-8B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B across in- and out-of-distribution settings by directly leveraging ranked preference data with choice models.

problem: Existing watermarking methods for LLM outputs require access to the decoding process, making them inapplicable to real-world settings like detecting AI-generated academic reviews where the model is unknown.
approach: In-Context Watermarking (ICW) embeds watermarks solely through prompt engineering, leveraging LLMs' in-context learning and instruction-following abilities, with detection methods paired to four granularity levels.
contribution: ICW is validated as a model-agnostic, practical watermarking approach offering scalable content attribution as LLMs become more capable.

problem: Identifying whether an LLM is trained from scratch or derived from a base model is difficult due to intensive post-training processes like fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and pruning that obscure model lineage.
approach: AWM proposes a training-free fingerprinting method leveraging weight matrices, Linear Assignment Problem, and centered kernel alignment (CKA) to neutralize parameter manipulations.
contribution: On 60 positive and 90 negative model pairs, AWM achieves perfect classification metrics with near-zero false positives and completes in 30 seconds on GPU.

problem: Self-rewarding methods for LLM reasoning suffer from training collapse due to single-view supervision signals forming self-consistent illusions, hindering label-free improvement of reasoning.
approach: Co-rewarding is a self-supervised RL framework seeking complementary supervision from different views: one via contrastive agreement across semantically analogous questions, another via slowly-updated reference teachers.
contribution: Co-rewarding exhibits stable training and achieves 3.31% average improvements on mathematical reasoning benchmarks over self-rewarding baselines.

problem: Precipitation nowcasting is challenging due to pronounced spatial locality, intricate fine-scale rainfall structures, and skewed benchmark datasets; diffusion models are computationally expensive while deterministic models remain biased toward normal rainfall.
approach: exPreCast is an efficient deterministic framework integrating local spatiotemporal attention, texture-preserving cubic dual upsampling, and temporal extraction, trained on a balanced radar dataset from KMA.
contribution: exPreCast achieves state-of-the-art performance on SEVIR, MeteoNet, and the balanced KMA dataset, delivering accurate nowcasts across ordinary and extreme precipitation events.

problem: Existing model-free RL algorithms achieve minimax regret bounds but have coarse gap-dependent bounds that fail to capture suboptimality gap structure.
approach: A novel analytical framework explicitly separates analysis of optimal and suboptimal state-action pairs, yielding fine-grained regret bounds for UCB-based and non-UCB-based Q-learning algorithms.
contribution: ULCB-Hoeffding, a new UCB-based algorithm, achieves fine-grained regret guarantees and empirically outperforms AMB; a refined AMB variant addresses truncation and martingale issues.

problem: LLM-based code agents for website generation rely only on simple code execution for feedback, failing to capture actual quality of generated code including visual effects and user interactions.
approach: WebGen-Agent leverages comprehensive multi-level visual feedback from screenshots and GUI-agent testing via a visual language model, combined with Step-GRPO using screenshot and GUI-agent scores as dense reward signals.
contribution: WebGen-Agent increases Claude 3.5 Sonnet accuracy from 26.4% to 51.9% and appearance score from 3.0 to 3.9 on WebGen-Bench, outperforming previous state-of-the-art.

problem: Out-of-distribution detection for NLP typically uses simple average-based aggregation of token embeddings, limiting effective use of token-level information.
approach: AP-OOD is a semi-supervised OOD detection method that flexibly interpolates between unsupervised and supervised settings by exploiting token-level information through attention pooling.
contribution: AP-OOD achieves state-of-the-art OOD detection: reducing FPR95 from 27.77% to 5.91% on XSUM and from 75.19% to 68.13% on WMT15 En-Fr.

problem: Bidirectional language models consistently outperform unidirectional models in context understanding, but the theoretical reason remains unclear.
approach: FlowNIB is a post-hoc framework adopting an information bottleneck perspective: bidirectional representations preserve more mutual information about input and target, yielding richer features; it estimates comparable MI values per layer.
contribution: Bidirectional LM layers exhibit higher mutual information than similar or larger unidirectional LMs, explaining their superior performance on GLUE, commonsense reasoning, and regression tasks.

problem: Improving reasoning ability in language models through RL is hindered by instability in training objectives and unclear connections between variational inference and RL methods.
approach: Variational Reasoning treats thinking traces as latent variables, optimizing via ELBO with a forward-KL formulation for stable posterior training; it unifies rejection sampling finetuning and GRPO as local forward-KL objectives.
contribution: The framework reveals implicit accuracy weighting in RL methods and provides stable, principled objectives validated on Qwen 2.5 and Qwen 3 across reasoning tasks.

problem: Multimodal LLMs fail in Abstract Visual Reasoning (AVR) tasks not primarily due to weak reasoning but due to absence of fine-grained visual perception.
approach: VisuRiddles provides an AVR benchmark from real-world data and a synthesizer generating AVR instances with perceptual descriptions and reasoning chains; PAVR employs two-stage training for perception then reasoning.
contribution: PAVR substantially outperforms open-source and commercial MLLMs on VisuRiddles, establishing fine-grained perception as the primary bottleneck in AVR.

problem: Robotic manipulation requires jointly learning visual representations and action policies, but existing approaches lack unified learning within a single framework or generalize poorly across embodiments.
approach: Genie Envisioner (GE) is a unified world foundation platform using an instruction-conditioned video diffusion model (GE-Base) for visual learning and a lightweight flow-matching decoder (GE-Act) for action policy.
contribution: Trained on over 1 million manipulation episodes, GE supports short- and long-horizon tasks and generalizes across embodiments with minimal supervision.

problem: Understanding what specific information-seeking goals drive readers during reading behavior has been unexplored, limiting development of educational and assistive technologies.
approach: Introduces goal decoding tasks using large-scale eye-tracking data in English, developing discriminative and generative multimodal LLMs to decode reader goals from eye movements and text.
contribution: Models show considerable success on goal selection from options and progress toward free-form textual reconstruction of precise goal formulations.

problem: Evaluating agent applications across heterogeneous domains lacks scalability and systematic accounting for user expertise and interaction quality beyond task correctness.
approach: TED framework (Talk, Evaluate, Diagnose) uses reusable expert/non-expert user personas, represents subgoals as natural language grading notes evaluated via LLM-as-a-judge, and provides automated error analysis.
contribution: TED reveals new performance insights across models and user expertise levels with new metrics capturing turn efficiency and intermediate progress.

problem: Photorealistic neural rendering requires unified treatment of object- and scene-level synthesis, but existing methods either use explicit 3D representations or rely on scarce labeled 3D data.
approach: Kaleido treats 3D as a specialized sub-domain of video as a sequence-to-sequence image synthesis task, using masked autoregressive framework with rectified flow transformer and leveraging large-scale video for pre-training.
contribution: Kaleido achieves state-of-the-art view synthesis on benchmarks, matches per-scene optimization quality in many-view settings, and substantially outperforms generative methods in few-view zero-shot.

problem: Existing mesh reconstruction methods suffer from texture concealing geometric errors and lack reliable mesh extraction with 3D supervision.
approach: DiMeR disentangles geometry and texture spaces: normal maps serve as sole input for geometry prediction while RGB informs texture, with streamlined mesh extraction and 3D supervision.
contribution: DiMeR generalizes across sparse-view, single-image, and text-to-3D tasks, reducing Chamfer Distance by over 30% on GSO and OmniObject3D.

problem: Video diffusion transformers struggle to generalize beyond training length due to attention dispersion and periodic content repetition in extrapolation.
approach: UltraViCo identifies attention dispersion as the unified cause of both failure modes and proposes a training-free suppression of attention for tokens beyond training window via constant decay factor.
contribution: UltraViCo pushes extrapolation limit from ~2x to 4x, improving Dynamic Degree and Imaging Quality by 233% and 40.5% respectively at 4x extrapolation.

problem: Existing code generation benchmarks rely on manual annotations, focus predominantly on Python, and suffer from limited difficulty and imbalanced language coverage.
approach: AutoCodeGen generates high-difficulty multilingual code datasets without manual annotations by generating test inputs with LLMs, obtaining outputs in sandbox, and filtering with multi-stage methods.
contribution: AutoCodeBench spans 20 languages with balanced coverage; experiments show state-of-the-art models struggle, particularly in low-resource languages.

problem: Time series anomaly detection relies primarily on unimodal numerical data, overlooking complementary information from other modalities.
approach: MindTS addresses semantic alignment across heterogeneous data via Fine-grained Time-text Semantic Alignment and Content Condenser Reconstruction for filtering redundancy and cross-modal interaction.
contribution: MindTS achieves competitive or superior results on six real-world multimodal datasets.

problem: Large language models frequently fail to recognize or address false presuppositions in cancer patient questions, posing risks to safe medical decision-making.
approach: Introduces Cancer-Myth, an expert-verified adversarial dataset of 585 cancer questions with false presuppositions, to systematically evaluate LLM failure on presupposition handling.
contribution: No frontier LLM corrects false presuppositions more than 43% of the time; mitigation strategies like prompting raise accuracy to 80% but cause misidentification in 41% of negatives.

problem: Generating high-quality neural network weights efficiently for diverse architectures faces challenges from high-dimensional weight spaces, network symmetries, and scaling to large models.
approach: DeepWeightFlow applies Flow Matching directly in weight space with Git Re-Basin and TransFusion for neural network canonicalization to handle permutation symmetries.
contribution: Generated networks achieve high accuracy without fine-tuning and scale to large architectures; ensembles of hundreds can be generated in minutes, far exceeding diffusion-based efficiency.

problem: Classifier-Free Guidance impact on sampling dynamics under multimodal conditionals remains poorly understood, limiting principled design of guidance schedules.
approach: Analysis shows three successive stages: Direction Shift (acceleration toward weighted mean), Mode Separation (bias suppresses weaker modes), and Concentration (amplified contraction), explaining the guidance-diversity tradeoff.
contribution: Theory predicts and experiments confirm that early strong guidance erodes global diversity while late strong guidance suppresses fine-grained variation; time-varying schedules improve both.

problem: Input-based explanations' effectiveness for promoting fairness in hate speech detection and their relationship with explainability remains unclear.
approach: First systematic study examines three dimensions: identifying biased predictions, selecting fair models, and mitigating bias during training, across encoder- and decoder-only models.
contribution: Input-based explanations effectively detect biased predictions and reduce training bias, but are unreliable for model selection; code released on GitHub.

problem: Current open-source visual captioning models have a large performance gap with commercial ones, limiting scalable applications like data synthesis.
approach: CapFlow is a multi-agent collaboration workflow leveraging open-source models to achieve GPT-4 caption quality; MetaCaptioner is a generalist captioner fine-tuned on CapFlow's synthetic captions.
contribution: MetaCaptioner achieves comparable quality to commercial models with 89.5% cost reduction; top-tier multimodal performance in open-source community.

problem: LLMs lack awareness of implicit authorial intents for writing and citation in long-form reports, limiting generation quality.
approach: Develops structured tag-based schemes to elicit underlying intents for writing and citing; enhanced intents improve both LLM zero-shot and enable high-quality synthetic data for fine-tuning.
contribution: Intent awareness improves performance by 2.9 and 12.3 absolute points for large and small models respectively; significantly improves citation usage and readability.

problem: Complex reasoning-intensive multimodal policies implemented as in-context prompts are increasingly lengthy, and existing policy compression work ignores reasoning depth and multimodal cases.
approach: Multimodal Policy Internalization (MPI) aims to internalize reasoning-intensive multimodal policies into model parameters via new datasets and algorithms for complex decision-making and tool-using tasks.
contribution: MPI enables stronger policy-following behavior without requiring policies in-context during inference across synthetic and real-world multimodal tasks.

problem: Multimodal LLMs' ability to comprehend immersive omnidirectional environments captured by 360x180 images remains unexplored.
approach: ODI-Bench provides 2,000 omnidirectional images and 4,000+ QA pairs across 10 fine-grained tasks; Omni-CoT enhances comprehension through chain-of-thought reasoning across textual and visual cues.
contribution: Benchmarking 20 MLLMs reveals current models struggle with immersive contexts; Omni-CoT significantly enhances omnidirectional understanding without training.

problem: SVD-based model merging methods rely on heuristically designed rank selection, leading to inter-task interference and suboptimal multi-task performance.
approach: AdaRank adaptively selects beneficial singular components of task vectors via per-component masks optimized on unlabeled test data with entropy minimization.
contribution: AdaRank consistently improves existing merging methods across diverse backbones from different modalities, largely narrowing performance gap with individually fine-tuned models.

problem: Existing reference-based image generation methods are limited to single-image references and cannot leverage 3D assets.
approach: RefAny3D is a cross-domain diffusion model using dual-branch perception of multi-view RGB images and point maps to jointly model colors and canonical-space coordinates.
contribution: Effectively uses 3D assets as references to produce images consistent with given assets, enabling new possibilities for combining diffusion with 3D content creation.

problem: Prototypical self-supervised learning methods suffer from partial prototype collapse where multiple prototypes converge to nearly identical representations.
approach: Fully decoupled training strategy learns prototypes and encoders under separate objectives: prototypes via online EM-style Gaussian mixture independent of encoder loss.
contribution: Eliminates prototype collapse without explicit regularization, yielding consistently diverse prototypes with improved downstream performance.

problem: Finetuned LLM-judges' real-world deployment ignores practical concerns of future-proofing, backward-compatibility, and generalization to unseen questions.
approach: Formalizes three aspects affecting shelf life of judges under unified framework: future-proofing (performance on future models), backward-compatibility (performance on past models), question generalization.
contribution: Future-proofing is challenging for most models; backward-compatibility is easier with DPO-trained models improving performance; continual learning provides balanced adaptation.

problem: Data selection for fine-tuning typically treats available target samples as validation sets, estimating data influence via single-sample removal, which is computationally costly.
approach: Train on Validation (ToV) inverts train-validation roles: performs inference on training pool before and after fine-tuning on validation set, selecting samples whose predictions change most.
contribution: Achieves lower test loss than state-of-the-art methods on instruction tuning and NER tasks with theoretical analysis.

problem: Vision-language models' spatial reasoning in realistic, unconstrained contexts with visual noise and diverse spatial relationships remains unexplored.
approach: SpatiaLab comprises 1,400 QA pairs across six categories (Relative Positioning, Depth & Occlusion, Orientation, Size & Scale, Spatial Navigation, 3D Geometry) with multiple-choice and open-ended evaluation.
contribution: Evaluation shows substantial gap between VLMs (InternVL3.5-72B: 54.93%) and humans (87.57%) in multiple-choice; all models show 10-25% performance drop in open-ended.

problem: Transformer LLMs' reasoning scaling with inference-time compute is hindered by constraints in forming task-optimal sequence representations within fixed attention mechanisms.
approach: Bottlenecked Transformers via periodic KV cache consolidation and reconsolidation (rewrites) following Information Bottleneck theory enables improved task-optimal representations.
contribution: Provides theoretical justification via IB theory for KV cache rewrites and demonstrates improved reasoning through memory consolidation.

problem: Modeling non-stationary processes where statistical properties vary across domains forces a trade-off between expressive but computationally demanding models and scalable but limited stationary methods.
approach: Random Wavelet Features (RWF) constructs scalable non-stationary kernel approximations by sampling from wavelet families, leveraging wavelets' localization and multi-resolution structure.
contribution: RWF outperforms stationary random features with convergence guarantees and unlocks scalable kernel methods for real-world non-stationary problems.

problem: Existing metadata for LLM pretraining acceleration focus only on URLs, leaving open whether other fine-grained metadata signals could yield greater efficiency benefits.
approach: Investigates wide range of metadata types, finds fine-grained document quality indicators accelerate pretraining when prepended; introduces metadata appending as auxiliary task.
contribution: Provides practical guidelines for integrating metadata; learnable meta-tokens with masked loss recover part of speedup by inducing quality-aware latent structure.

problem: AI systems struggle to design and execute complex end-to-end data-lake-to-insight pipelines requiring orchestration of multiple data tasks.
approach: KramaBench consists of 104 challenges spanning 1700 files, 24 data sources, and 6 domains; DS-Guru framework tests end-to-end pipeline design and task implementation via LLMs and agentic systems.
contribution: Best system reaches only 50% end-to-end accuracy; even with perfect retrieval accuracy tops 59%, revealing critical gaps in pipeline orchestration.

problem: Direct reasoning over long, noisy documents remains brittle and error-prone for QA tasks; reliable verification requires consolidating dispersed evidence into structured outputs.
approach: LiteCoST framework uses Chain-of-Structured-Thought (CoST) template for strong LLMs to generate structured outputs with steps, then fine-tunes SLMs via supervised tuning and GRPO with dual rewards.
contribution: Achieves LLM-comparable quality on finance and legal long-document QA with 3B/7B SLMs, delivering 2-4x lower latency than GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1.

problem: Recent feature caching methods for diffusion acceleration suffer from severe quality loss by failing to model complex feature evolution dynamics.
approach: HiCache uses Hermite polynomial-based feature caching with dual-scaling mechanism for numerical stability; training-free plug-in acceleration framework.
contribution: Achieves 5.55x speedup on FLUX.1-dev while exceeding baseline quality; effective on text-to-image, video, and super-resolution; improves ClusCa from 0.9480 to 0.9840.
